To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The use of resistively loaded frequency selective surfaces in thin electromagnetic absorbers allows to achieve wideband absorption with a reduced thickness”.
A thin electromagnetic absorber is designed by using resistively-loaded high impedance surfaces.
We have demonstrated that thin electromagnetic absorbers can be designed by using high-impedance surfaces loaded with resistors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the absorbing properties of resistively loaded high impedance surfaces.
the design and analysis of a new ultra thin electromagnetic absorber based on a resistive loaded frequency selective surface.
the analysis and design of ultra-thin absorbing screens comprising resistively loaded high impedance surfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimum surface resistance of the HIS absorber depends on the thickness of the substrate and on the FSS element geometry.
the proposed absorber, despite its thin profile, exhibits a very wide absorption bandwidth and a high absorption level.

a wideband absorber with a reduced thickness is obtained when a resistive HIS is designed with the following characteristics: (i) the FSS element is square, (ii) the surface resistance is about 0.5 Ohms, (iii) the substrate thickness is 0.1λ0.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to design a very thin absorber with a very wideband behavior.
we have shown the feasibility of using resistive FSS to design thin absorbers with a very wide absorption bandwidth.
the proposed structure, which is very thin (less than 1/20 wavelength), exhibits a very wideband behavior (from 1.8 GHz up to 12 GHz) in terms of absorption, and a very low reflection level.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a thin absorber with a wideband response can be designed by using a lossy FSS comprising square patches printed on a dielectric substrate with a thickness of a quarter wavelength at the central frequency of operation.
the absorption performance of a thin absorber is mainly dependent on the surface resistance of its FSS and that a wideband absorption in thin absorbers can be achieved with resistive FSS.
the absorber can be designed to absorb a wide bandwidth of frequencies by properly choosing the shape of the FSS element and the surface resistance.
